name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deeply Democratic district with a +29 partisan lean
Incumbent Menefee well-funded with no outside opposition spending
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: TX-18's +29 Democratic lean, Menefee's incumbency and strong fundraising against an underfunded Republican challenger make this a Safe Democratic hold; markets agree at roughly 96%.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Menefee would be the first sign of movement, though none is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-18 is a heavily Democratic Houston-area seat with a partisan lean of about 29 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Christian Menefee, first elected in a 2025 special election cycle, is running for a full term and has raised over $3.6 million, with more than $7 million in outside support and no recorded outside spending against him.

Republican Ronald Whitfield reports no fundraising or cash on hand. No public polls cover the race, but prediction markets give Menefee roughly a 96% chance of winning. With fundamentals this lopsided and a weak-funded challenger, the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
